title: Add LCA repair to fix rounds — correlated failures repair the shared parent decomposition
description:

ATG (arXiv 2607.01942; plan: _plans/2026-07-12-bead-io-contract.md §Deferred) shows the higher-leverage move: trace correlated failures to their lowest common ancestor in the decomposition (shared epic/plan), repair the decomposition once, regenerate that subgraph, and keep verified beads frozen. Design where this hooks in (ac-review fix rounds, ac-batch-close) now that the Delivers/Consumes contract makes 'which beads are poisoned' a graph walk.

- [ ] Design note: detection rule for 'correlated failure' (shared root cause across 2+ beads) and the escalation path to parent-level repair
- [ ] ac-review and/or ac-batch-close fix-round procedure updated to escalate correlated failures to the shared parent instead of per-bead patches
- [ ] Frozen-region rule stated: closed+verified beads are never reopened by the repair; downstream Consumes lines identify what must be re-checked

title: Two-tier Agent Mail identity model — doctrine + wiring (ratified 2026-07-14)
description:
DECISION (Craig, 2026-07-14, this session): adopt the TWO-TIER identity model, replacing agent-identity.md's unwired mint-or-inherit doctrine. Rationale recorded so this isn't relitigated:
- Identity is the lock grain; the grain must match the WRITER-CONCURRENCY boundary. At PARALLEL_WIDTH>1 the parallel ac-implement children are independent concurrent writers in one shared checkout — inheriting one loop identity would put multiple writers under one name (forbidden by agent-identity.md's own corollary). Below the boundary, workers never commit/reserve, so per-worker identity is pure ceremony. The inherit model was written for a serial world; the width dial obsoleted it.
- TIER 1 (unique minted identity — mint via macro_start_session, reserve at work grain, release, self-deregister at exit): any session that CLAIMS BEADS or EDITS PRODUCT CODE — loop conductor (claims only), each ac-implement child, ac-review (auto-fix engineer edits code), ac-batch-close (fix-forward). Plan-family skills already conform.
- TIER 2 (FoggyCreek as EXPLICIT shared chore identity, not accidental fallback): serial low-contention writers — scheduled jobs (tidy/align/dream), ac-land sweep/report commits. HARD RULE = tier boundary AND safety guard: FoggyCreek may commit chore files but may NEVER claim beads or reserve files.
- Deregistration = 3 layers: (1) minter self-deregisters at own exit; (2) ac-land sweeps the identity roster handed by the loop (VERIFIED 2026-07-14 against live schemas: deregister_agent/retire_agent take registration_token as OPTIONAL — sweep by name works; force_release_file_reservation exists for stale holds); (3) next-run Phase-0 stale sweep + reservation TTL floor.
- Claim-visibility chain (CLAIM_ASSIGNEE threading + beads-closed-gate union + fail-closed) is solid and UNCHANGED by this epic.
Audit that produced this: 5 gaps — exit-land can't release/deregister identities never handed to it; stages never deregister; agent-identity.md contradicts live per-stage model; engineer wip-commit hatch collides with pre-commit guard; FoggyCreek fallback silently misattributes claims. Children implement; doctrine-rewrite child blocks the rest.

DECISION: prefix keeps the ratified decision card (decision/options/context, 15s rule). NEW: ACTION: prefix + action-card template for do-in-the-world items (fields: what / where / checklist / estimated time / best-done-when). human-gate remains the SOLE gate label (cockpit predicates untouched). Motivating example: BCA bd-l6khg.13 (ASC intro-offer config — no options, pure action, must ride a version submission). Update SKILL.md + reference/human-gate-template.md; docket consumers (ac-human-session, cockpit) sort by prefix.

title: Extend ac-implement close ritual: stamp worker model/session identity per bead at close

Stamp worker model id + session name on each bead at close (structured comment or field) so future model-level comparisons are joinable. Touches ac-implement (close ritual) + beads-standards note.

title: Extend beads-standards/bead-conventions: per-type close-artifact shapes (bug/investigation/task close with typed evidence)
description: Craig green-light 2026-07-15: formalize what each issue_type closes WITH — bug: repro + fix evidence + regression test ref; investigation: findings + spawned beads; task: delivered artifact refs. Extends the structured close_reason canon (outcome verbs) one level down so closed beads cluster/segment cleanly for future metrics. comments.author: craigvanheerden
comments.text: SCOPE TRIMMED (Craig 80/20 review, 2026-07-15): NO new template machinery. title: Fix ac-land defaults conflict: 'leave local Supabase running' vs the loop-close CI dispatch's stack guard on self-hosted runners
description:
DECISION (reframed from bug by ac-bead-refine 2026-07-16 RUN 20260716-111224-31570): the incident is real but the bead's prescribed fix target has been retired -- this needs a human / cross-repo scoping call before any implementation.

## Context (verified 2026-07-16)
Filed as a bug: ac-land's teardown leaves the local Supabase stack running, and the loop-close quality-gate CI dispatch then FAILS at its 'Supabase local stack guard' step (BCA loop run 20260714-170945-6308; workflow run 29415325669 failed, re-dispatch 29422885351 green after stopping the stack). The incident is real. But the prescribed fix location no longer exists in the canonical skill:

- ac-land NO LONGER fires any loop-close / full-suite CI dispatch. That trigger was retired in commit 6473d5e ("refactor(ac-land,ac-loop): retire the loop-close full-suite trigger", bd-pwt44, 2026-07-13 -- two days BEFORE the cited incident). The full-suite proof moved to PUBLISH START via ac-prove (`ac-publish` -> `ac-prove ensure --fix-forward`). skills/ac-land/SKILL.md:288-296 now states plainly "no CI dispatch, nothing to wait on."
- The string 'Supabase local stack guard' (and 'Supabase' generally) appears NOWHERE in agent-compounds. The guard step lives in a CI workflow (quality-gate.yml) that is NOT in this repo -- it is in the consuming app repo (BCA) / infrastructure. This repo has only lint.yml.
- The bead's "~line 517+" citation points at unrelated /tmp artifact-cleanup code; the real Teardown section (line ~593) has no Supabase/CI logic either.

So the bead's binding sections rest on retired / cross-repo state (present-tree-rule violation, bead-conventions.md).

## The fork (only a human / cross-repo owner can resolve)
Where -- if anywhere -- does the local-Supabase-stack <-> CI-guard collision still occur after bd-pwt44, and which repo owns the fix?

## Options
- A. SUPERSEDED -- close as fixed-by-bd-pwt44. If ac-land no longer fires a land-time dispatch, the exact collision described (teardown-leaves-stack -> land-time dispatch) can no longer originate from ac-land. Caveat: the incident POST-dates the retirement, so a dispatch did fire on 2026-07-15 from somewhere.
- B. RETARGET to ac-prove / publish-start. If the collision now happens at `ac-prove ensure --fix-forward`'s dispatch, the stop-local-stack ordering belongs in ac-prove (or ac-publish) teardown, not ac-land. Re-scope the bead's file + ACs there.
- C. RETARGET to the CI workflow (cross-repo). The 'Supabase local stack guard' step is defined in a quality-gate.yml OUTSIDE agent-compounds. If the guard should tolerate / stop a local stack on self-hosted runners, the fix is in that workflow (BCA / infrastructure), not in any agent-compounds skill.
- D. STALE-SYMLINK hypothesis -- the 2026-07-15 BCA run consumed an un-synced older ac-land copy that still fired the dispatch. If so, the fix is a re-sync + verify symlink freshness; the doctrine change already landed. Close as superseded.

## Recommendation (agent)
Investigate BCA run 29415325669's origin FIRST -- which workflow + step fired it, and from which skill copy. Most likely B or D. Do NOT implement the bead as written: its ac-land teardown target is retired. Route the fix to whichever repo/skill the investigation identifies as the true owner.

## Delivers
- decision: which repo/skill owns the local-stack <-> CI-guard fix (or a close-as-superseded record), plus the origin of BCA run 29415325669

comments.text: Reframed bug->decision + human-gate by ac-bead-refine (RUN 20260716-111224-31570). 2-reviewer consensus + conductor verification: fix target retired. ac-land no longer fires a loop-close CI dispatch (bd-pwt44 / 6473d5e, 2026-07-13); 'Supabase local stack guard' string absent from this repo; guard lives in a cross-repo quality-gate.yml. title: Fix 2 lint conformance fails: dangling /ac-tidy-run xref + 'canonical_ingredients' portability violation
description:
Maintenance heartbeat 2026-07-16 `./lint.sh` (309 checks, 4 fails). Two of the four are owned by this bead (the other 2 README fails are ac-7zb):

Check 2 (/ac-* xref resolution): `FAIL: /ac-tidy-run referenced in skills but skills/ac-tidy-run/ does not exist`. ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-07-16): the sole occurrence of the token is a **temp-directory name**, not a skill cross-reference -- `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:35`: `TIDY_WT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ac-tidy-run-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-$$"`. Check 2's regex `/ac-[a-z][a-z-]*[a-z]` matches the `/ac-tidy-run` path segment and treats it as a slash-command invocation. No skill named ac-tidy-run exists or is intended. Fix = make the temp-dir token stop matching the xref regex; do NOT restore/create a skill.

Check 6 (portability): `FAIL: portability violation 'canonical_ingredients' found in skills/_shared/qa-shared.md`. Verified: qa-shared.md:49 -- "...mutates cross-user shared data -- canonical_ingredients zone gates, the...". The token is a body-compass-app-specific identifier that must not appear in portable shared skill text.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `cd /Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/neometa/software/agent-compounds`
2. `./lint.sh 2>&1 | grep FAIL`
3. Observe the two FAIL lines above (plus the 2 README fails owned by ac-7zb).

## Approach (advisory)
- Check 2: rename the temp-dir token in skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:35 so it no longer matches `/ac-[a-z...]` -- e.g. drop the leading-slash `/ac-` shape (`tidy-run-...`, `ac_tidy_run-...`, or `actidy-run-...`). Grep confirms line 35 is the sole referrer; the variable must still yield a unique per-run path. Do NOT create skills/ac-tidy-run/.
- Check 6: replace `canonical_ingredients` in skills/_shared/qa-shared.md:49 with portable phrasing (e.g. "a canonical shared-data zone" / "shared-data tables") preserving the sentence's meaning without the app-specific token.
- Per the maintenance protocol these were filed as a finding rather than fixed inline; ac-implement applies the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md no longer contains a `/ac-tidy-run` token; the temp-dir variable still produces a unique per-run path.
- [ ] `./lint.sh` Check 2 emits zero FAILs (verify: `./lint.sh 2>&1 | sed -n '/Check 2/,/Check 3/p'`).
- [ ] skills/_shared/qa-shared.md contains no `canonical_ingredients` token; the sentence's meaning is preserved.
- [ ] `./lint.sh` Check 6 emits zero FAILs.

(Note -- NOT gated by this bead's diff: ac-k9g's two Check-specific ACs above fully verify its own two-file diff. Separately, once ac-7zb also lands, `./lint.sh` reaches 0 total failures -- but that end-state depends on ac-7zb's disjoint README fix, so it is a cross-reference, not a checkbox for this bead.)

## Test Scope
- Command: `./lint.sh` -- Check 2 (xref resolution) and Check 6 (portability greps). The lint script is the check; no unit test.
- Files touched: skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md, skills/_shared/qa-shared.md.
- Modality: tooling/skill-text change, no app user surface -> lint-command verification only.

## Delivers
- file: skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md -- temp-dir token renamed off the /ac-* pattern
- file: skills/_shared/qa-shared.md -- 'canonical_ingredients' replaced with portable phrasing

## Consumes
- none
